[short] skip 'does a build in using an empty cache'

# Start with a fresh cache because we want to verify the behavior
# when the tool hasn't been cached previously.
env GOCACHE=$WORK${/}cache

# The go command keeps no executable cache: 'go tool -n' builds the tool and
# prints where it put it, the build's own directory, never the cache.
# A cold run links into the action's exe directory; a warm one names the
# action directory itself. Both sit under the build's own work directory.
go tool -n foo
stdout 'go-build[0-9]+[/\\].*foo'$GOEXE'$'
! stdout $GOCACHE

# A later run builds from the cached package and prints its own location.
go tool -n foo
stdout 'go-build[0-9]+[/\\].*foo'$GOEXE'$'
! stdout $GOCACHE

-- go.mod --
module example.com/foo

go 1.25

tool example.com/foo
-- main.go --
package main

func main() {}
